sentence: This project builds public software that predicts non-normal protein sequences of cancer cells from DNA or RNA data and confirms them with mass spectrometry.
This project studies how computer-aided detection of tuberculosis on chest X-rays works for screening in communities, including its accuracy, barriers and cost.
This project studies how lymphatic endothelial cell junctions and drainage are controlled, using a bioengineered 3D lymphatic vascular system and mouse models of lymphedema.
This project collects and reports cancer statistics, such as how often cancer occurs and how long patients survive, and tracks changes in cancer rates.
This project studies how different amacrine cell types in the retina shape the responses of ganglion cells through inhibitory interactions, using mice.
This project studies how two inhibitory receptors affect T cell exhaustion during chronic viral infection, using mice infected with a virus.
This project builds a genetically engineered mouse strain with more mucosal-associated invariant T cells to study how these cells develop and function.
This project studies how a molecular switch reprograms the immune surroundings of prostate cancer tumors through transcriptional and chromatin remodeling mechanisms.
This project builds three platforms for sensing molecules and imaging biological systems, using optical spectroscopy, nanofabrication and machine learning.
This project builds and tests imaging, optical and molecular technologies and computer methods to improve cancer detection, diagnosis and therapy.
This project studies how coronaviruses recognize receptors and enter cells, at the molecular and structural level.
This project searches for drugs to treat Alzheimer's disease and related disorders, using drug discovery and chemistry facilities.
This project tests whether a positron emission tomography tracer can diagnose lung tumors that resist therapy, and targets their mitochondrial metabolism.
This project studies DNA and RNA features of tumors from patients at many cancer centers to find which ones match clinical outcomes.
This project builds a machine learning method that uses CT images and patient characteristics to predict cancer spread to cervical lymph nodes.
This project studies how moving homes and housing insecurity affect the health of older adults with cancer.
This project studies how a transcription factor shapes the development of skull bones and their sutures, and its link to craniosynostosis.
This project builds a computer model of how drug molecules interact with biomolecules, to help design drugs that target a particular signaling pathway.
This project uses mouse models to find out how somatic mutations cause an inflammatory and hematologic disease and how it might be treated.
This project tries to find out whether gut microbiome differences predict how cancer patients respond to immune checkpoint blockade, and whether fecal microbiota transplant helps.
